title: The morning a mountain lost 1,300 feet 🌋
subject: volcano
description:
Would you have stayed outside the red zone? 👇

On May 18, 1980, Mount St. Helens in Washington lost its summit in the largest landslide ever recorded. Its ash turned day into night 250 miles away and circled the planet in 15 days.

Sources: USGS Fact Sheet 036-00, "Mount St. Helens: From the 1980 Eruption to 2000"; HISTORY, "Mount St. Helens" (updated May 2025); Wikipedia, "1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens".

scenes.text: One Sunday morning, a mountain lost 1,300 feet of height.
Mount St. Helens, Washington, May 18, 1980. At 8:32 a.m., a 5.1 earthquake shook it.
Within 20 seconds, the whole north face slid away, the largest landslide ever recorded.
A sideways blast flattened forest across 230 square miles.
Ash shot 15 miles up in 15 minutes, and Spokane, 250 miles away, fell into complete darkness.
57 people died. The ash crossed the United States in 3 days and circled Earth in 15.
